core_obligations: Record that part (1) is immediate from the definitions and that part (3) is a formal consequence of part (2) together with the cited lemma computing cohomology with support (proof lines 8559-8562).

View i as a morphism of ringed spaces (Z, O_X|_Z) -> (X, O_X) and note that i_* is exact and that i^* = i^{-1} is exact with i^*i_* isomorphic to the identity, so that i_* is fully faithful on the derived level with left inverse i^{-1} (proof lines 8565-8577).

For K in D_Z(O_X), use exactness of i_* and i^{-1} to reduce the adjunction map K -> i_*i^{-1}K to the level of cohomology sheaves; since those sheaves are supported on Z the maps are isomorphisms, so i_* is an equivalence (proof lines 8577-8584).
Conclude the identification of the quasi-inverse by writing K = i_*i^{-1}K for K in D_Z(O_X) and invoking the cited lemma on cohomology with support (proof lines 8586-8591).
proof_roadmap: Dispose of parts (1) and (3) by definition and formal consequence.
Establish full faithfulness of i_* from exactness of the adjoint pair for a closed immersion.
Show the adjunction unit is an isomorphism on supported complexes via cohomology sheaves.
Identify R-H_Z with i^{-1} on the supported derived category.
difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes three facts for the inclusion i : Z -> X of a closed subset: that i_* lands in D_Z(O_X), that i_* : D(O_X|_Z) -> D_Z(O_X) is an equivalence with quasi-inverse i^{-1} = R-H_Z on D_Z, and that i_* composed with R-H_Z is right adjoint to the inclusion D_Z(O_X) -> D(O_X). The substantive part is the equivalence: it uses exactness of i_* and i^* = i^{-1} for a closed immersion to get full faithfulness, then proves the adjunction map K -> i_*i^{-1}K is an isomorphism for K supported on Z by reducing to cohomology sheaves and applying the support hypothesis (proof lines 8565-8584). The final identification R-H_Z(K) = i^{-1}K on D_Z then reduces to the cited computation on the support (proof lines 8586-8591). H3: an equivalence of triangulated categories proved through adjunction and cohomology-sheaf reduction is research-level, not a routine formal consequence.
